jobDescription: A business-accounting software company sells monthly subscriptions to small firms and offers a free trial before the first payment. The experimentation team helps product squads design, run and read A/B tests on the signup and trial journeys, and it keeps the metric definitions that every readout uses. The Data Scientist will plan tests, check randomisation and sample ratios, write readouts with confidence intervals and teach squads how to read them. The team also values methods work that has been published or presented outside the company.
requirements: Plans A/B tests with a pre-declared primary metric, a power calculation and a fixed test window.
Writes experiment readouts that report the effect against control with a confidence interval.
Checks randomisation quality, including sample-ratio mismatch, before a readout is published.
Maintains governed metric definitions in a metrics layer and documents how they change over time.
Has published or presented methods work in experimentation or causal inference.

evidence.text: Planned 23 A/B tests on the signup and trial journeys at Ledgerline, writing each plan with a primary metric, a power calculation and a fixed test window before launch.

Wrote the readout for the trial-reminder email test: trial-to-paid conversion was 6.2% in control and 7.0% in treatment over 4 to 31 March 2024, a difference of 0.8 points with a 95% interval of 0.3 to 1.3 points.
Added an automated sample-ratio check to the readout notebook template that blocks publication when the observed split departs from the plan by more than the agreed threshold.
Moved the trial and conversion metric definitions into the dbt semantic layer so that every squad computed conversion the same way.
Ran a monthly drop-in clinic where product managers brought draft readouts for review before sharing them.

Work sample: the anonymised readout for the trial-reminder email test, containing the pre-registered plan, the sample-ratio check (49.8% and 50.2%), conversion by arm (6.2% and 7.0%), the confidence interval and the product director's sign-off.

Recruiter verification: the workshop paper 'Variance reduction for subscription trials with pre-period covariates' was located in the published proceedings of the 2023 Workshop on Causal Inference in Industry, which list the candidate as second author; the proceedings page was saved to the candidate file.
HR verification note: the candidate's employment at Ledgerline from August 2020 to June 2024 with the title Data Scientist was confirmed through the employer's third-party verification service.
